summary: FMT is a Dutch maker of food-processing machines based in 's-Hertogenbosch. For fresh potatoes and other root crops it builds receiving, destoning, washing, peeling, inspection, transport, storage and filling equipment, and says it offers complete lines for fresh potatoes. Its screw destoner is stated to handle up to 8 tons/hour.
machines: Box tipping system: stainless steel tipper that empties boxes of potatoes and root crops
Screw de-stoner: water-filled hopper and vertical screw that removes stones and earth
Drum washing machine: rod drum that cleans potatoes with water and tumbling
Continuous roller peeler: abrasive rollers in a drum peel potatoes and other root crops
Batch peeler: abrasive surface removes skin batch by batch
Vibration dewatering system: removes water and spreads product along the line
Roller inspection table IRT: rotates product for visual quality inspection
Transport screws and belt conveyors: move product between machines
Underwater storage tank: stores product under water, also used as a dip tank
Bag filling unit: fills bags or crates by weight or by volume
markets: Medium-sized and large international food processing companies
Agents in 21 locations across Asia, the Middle East, Europe and Australia
facts: Supplying machines for vegetables, fruit and meat processing for over twenty five years
Screw destoner capacity up to 8 tons/hour, depending on product size
Continuous abrasive peeler: about 800 kg/hour peeled, about 3,200 kg/hour input with about 25% waste
Roller inspection table lengths 2,000 mm to 5,000 mm
limitations: Founding year, legal form, ownership, employee numbers, turnover and factory location are not published on the pages read.
No customers, installations or export countries are named, and most potato machines have no published model number or capacity.
